cards.explanation: The answer is no cluster to eat. Micah says, "there is no cluster to eat, no early fig that I crave." He compares himself to someone gleaning a vineyard, and that gleaner comes up with no cluster. It's like reaching into the cookie box at the end of the party and feeling nothing but crumbs.

The answer is that they hunt one another with a net. Micah says, "They all lie in wait for blood; they hunt one another with a net." A net is what you'd think of for hunting animals, and here the people hunt one another. I'll say it plainly, friends: this part is heavy.

The answer is False. Micah doesn't say a few. He says, "They all lie in wait for blood; they hunt one another with a net." He says it right after he says "there is no one upright among men." It's a heavy verse, and "all" is the word it uses.

The answer is bribe. Micah says, "the prince and the judge demand a bribe." A judge is the one who's supposed to be fair, and this one has his hand out. That's a referee checking his pocket before he blows the whistle. I think that's a heavy thing to see in the leaders.

The answer is True. Micah says, "When the powerful utters his evil desire, they all conspire together." One powerful person speaks his evil desire, and then they all conspire together. That's exactly what the verse says.

The answer is a brier. Micah says, "The best of them is like a brier…" A brier is a thorny bush, the kind that snags your sleeve when you walk by. So even the top of the list is prickly, friends. Micah doesn't have one smooth, friendly option to point to.

The answer is False. Micah says, "The day for your watchmen has come, the day of your visitation." He doesn't say it's a long way off, because it has come. Then he says, "Now is the time of their confusion." Both of those sound like the present.

The answer is the one who lies in your arms. Micah says, "Seal the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your arms." Right before that, he says not to rely on a friend or trust in a companion. Then he points to someone in your arms. It's a heavy line.

The answer is household. Micah says, "A man’s enemies are the members of his own household." He's been listing family: a son, a daughter, a daughter-in-law. I think this is the part of the passage that hurts most. These are the people who should be on your side, and the text says otherwise.

The answer is that Micah will look to the LORD and wait. He says, "But as for me, I will look to the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation." Everyone around him is a risk, so he looks up instead of around. I think that's a big breath after a heavy passage, friends. And he doesn't just look, he waits.

The answer is True, and it's a good place to end. The last words in the passage are "My God will hear me." After all those verses about people who can't be trusted, Micah is still sure about that. He's not guessing, and he's not just hoping. He says it flat out.
